speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance with regard to the rising use of Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) schemes among young consumers (a) what regulations govern BNPL schemes to address the potential risks associated with easy access to large purchases; (b) how is appropriate credit assessment of young users ensured before approving their use of such platforms; (c) whether their outstanding BNPL payments are factored into total debt servicing ratio calculations; and (d) how are youths educated on responsible BNPL usage and financial prudence.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MAS provided details on the safeguards in the BNPL Code in our past replies to Parliamentary Questions in November 2022 and more recently, in February this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These account for 98% of all credit granted to Singapore households by commercial entities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: MoneySense, our national financial education programme, shares content on the importance of money management and financial budgeting on its website and social media channels.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: These include advising consumers to beware of spending beyond their means while using BNPL schemes and other instalment plans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The national school curriculum from primary up to the tertiary level has incorporated key financial concepts, such as the effects of compound interest and the responsible use of credit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The efforts are complemented by talks and exhibitions organised for youths by MoneySense.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I understand it is only 1% but considering the take-up of such services, and I am more concerned about youths and young adults, and the growing popularity of BNPL schemes, does MAS foresee the necessity for stricter regulatory frameworks beyond the existing Code of Conduct?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And what proactive steps are being considered to adapt to potential future challenges posed by BNPL schemes?

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think we need to look at it in three parts.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: First, the responsibility of the regulator, in this case MAS, the responsibility of the industry and the responsibility of the individual borrower.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On MAS' part, as the regulator, as I mentioned, MAS has provided guidance on the development of the BNPL Code.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: It has also worked with MoneySense, the financial education programme, to encourage users to spend within their means.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: MAS will continue to monitor the BNPL sector and its development, and review the regulatory framework, as appropriate.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: On the industry's part, the code has already been in place since 2023.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: I think it is also important that borrowers and individuals also bear responsibility for their own individual purchases.

speaker: Mr Alvin Tan
text: There is a good CNA article about the BNPL issue and it spoke about the different purchases, particularly made by youths and young people in spending what they want and what they need.
